text:
marta: Heads-up: deploybot applied a pin after elevated error counts on runtime-4.0 for the "edgefilters" model family. We need a split-rollout unpin that avoids dedicated tenants and noisy-batch jobs.

deploybot: [automated] sticky pin created. pin_id=pb-2025-05-10-42. Affected: model-family 'edgefilters' (edgefilter-xl, edgefilter-fast). Trigger: error_rate > 2% sustained (10m). See /pins/pb-2025-05-10-42 for metadata.

nadir: I scanned traces — failures cluster on GPU OOMs from mixed-batch pipelines and from long context (>12k). Short inference appears fine.

elaine: Proposal: do a split unpin by route and by seq-length. Canary on non-dedicated read routes with max_seq<=4096, then expand to short-batch production traffic. Exclude: any route tagged `dedicated` or `batch-heavy`.

chris: Agree. Also let's use header-based routing so we can tag synthetic tests. We should mark canary traffic with `X-Canary-Pin: pb-2025-05-10-42-unpin` so logs are searchable.

marta: Ops, can deploybot do a split unpin that both excludes labels and applies traffic tagging?

ops-sre-bot: Yes. Example commands in runbook. Suggested sequence:
1) tag canary hosts `pin_canary=pb-2025-05-10-42`
2) canary unpin command (region us-central, exclude dedicated & batch):
```bash
deploybot unpin --pin pb-2025-05-10-42 \
  --scope region:us-central \
  --traffic-filter "max_seq<=4096 AND route:!=dedicated AND tag:!=batch-heavy" \
  --request-headers "X-Canary-Pin:pb-2025-05-10-42-unpin" \
  --mode canary
```
3) run synthetic and quick-eval suite for 15m, look at `error_rate`, `oom_rate`, `p99_latency`, `model_accuracy_regressions`
4) if green -> expand to short-batch (max_seq<=8192) for non-dedicated routes, monitor 30m -> full unwind.

nadir: Rollback criteria suggestion: any of the following within 15m -> rollback: oom_rate > 0.5%, error_rate increases > 0.8pp from baseline, or p99_latency > baseline * 1.25.

chris: I'll push a lightweight traffic generator that sends the `X-Canary-Pin` header and checks deterministic responses. Will post script here.

marta: Release notes: include the pin id, affected model family, and the exclusion for dedicated pools. @elaine can you add a short entry and notify PMs?

elaine: Yep. Draft for release tracker: "Temporary sticky pin pb-2025-05-10-42 applied to runtime-4.0 for edgefilters due to GPU OOMs on large-context/batch jobs. Scoped canary unpin planned; dedicated and batch-heavy routes excluded. See runbook."

ops-sre-bot: Ops checklist:
- Ensure canary label on hosts
- Run canary unpin command above at scheduled time 03:00 UTC
- Run `chris` synthetic suite and kpis for 15m
- Decision point at +15m -> expand or rollback
- Final unwind target by 05:00 UTC if green

chris: synthetic driver (bash):
```bash
for i in {1..1000}; do
  curl -s -H "X-Canary-Pin: pb-2025-05-10-42-unpin" \
    "https://canary-edge/api/generate?model=edgefilter-fast&max_seq=1024" > resp.$i.json &
done
wait
# quick metrics
jq -s '[.[]] | {errors: map(select(.status!=200))|length, p99: (map(.latency)|sort)[int(length*0.99)] }' resp.*.json
```

nadir: Also add a short correctness check: sample 50 responses and run the regression tests suite `tools/eval/edgefilter_smoke.py` against them.

marta: Who will own the canary monitoring and decision?

elaine: I'll be primary oncall and will call the decision. chris will operate synthetic runs, nadir will monitor infra traces.

ops-sre-bot: Scheduling note: deploybot can schedule the canary unpin at 03:00 UTC if this channel approves. React with :eyes: to approve automated run.

marta: Approved. :eyes:

chris: ack and will post run logs here during the window.

nadir: I'll watch traces and post any anomaly snippets.

elaine: I'll update the release tracker and DM customer success about the targeted window.

marta: Thanks. If rollback needed, use `deploybot pin --pin pb-2025-05-10-42 --force` and call the #oncall line. Keep notes in incident log.

ops-sre-bot: Closing planning thread and will reopen with canary results. Good luck.
